reason: Every assertion checks a parse error of Playwright's `role=` selector string: an empty role, an unknown attribute, a `level` or `checked` value of the wrong type, `~=` on a non-string value, `level` on a role it doesn't support, and an attribute with no value. Strider's `getByRole` takes typed options, so there's no selector string to parse and no parse error to raise. Each invalid value is a type error at compile time

Both set `process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_INERT_CHECK` or `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_DIALOG_CHECK` and skip on every `mode` but `default`, because Playwright's in-process server reads the variable when it starts. They test that switch of Playwright's injected script, which Strider doesn't have: its `getByRole` always applies the inert and modal-dialog rules that these switches turn off
